summary: Utility that converts a bit index into a bitmask byte pair: writes the byte offset (a1 >> 3) through output pointer a2, computes the single-bit mask 1 << (a1 & 7), stores that mask through output byte a3, and returns it. Callers such as sub_584230, sub_586800 and sub_586AA0 (e.g. the MultiBlockBitfieldEncoder bitmap loop) use it to map a linear bit index onto a caller-owned bitmap byte array.

local_names.a2: output pointer receiving the byte offset of the bit
local_names.a3: output byte receiving the single-bit mask
local_names.result: the bit mask 1 << (a1 & 7), both stored and returned

operations.description: Writes the byte offset of the bit: *a2 = a1 >> 3, i.e. the high bits of the bit index select the target byte within the caller's bitmap array
Builds the single-bit mask: result = 1 << (a1 & 7), i.e. the low 3 bits of the bit index select the bit position inside the byte
Stores the computed mask into the output byte: *a3 = result
Returns the bit mask byte; callers include sub_584230 (0x00584230), sub_586800 (0x00586800) and sub_586AA0 (0x00586AA0)

unresolved: Whether a2/a3 point into a caller-owned bitmap byte array (suggested by a1 >> 3) is DERIVED from usage, not stated by packet facts
The signed char return value and the *a3 output are the same mask, so callers may consume either
